alignments.note: Presentative imperative rendered by the single word Behold.
Adjunctive kai realized by also, displaced after the noun phrase; rule 15 permits the reordering.
Article to the under rule 19; rule 26 keeps it separate from its noun.
Noun stands alone, its determiner having gone to the article.

Correlative adjective telikauta rendered by the two-word so great. Head on great as the meaning-bearing word under rule 17; a head on so, which spells the correlative element, is the competing reading, but great is what the lexeme's magnitude sense answers to, and rule 99's what manner of frame is not the parallel because great is not a supplied generic completion.

Circumstantial participle of eimi expanded into a finite concessive clause. The supplied subordinator though and the supplied subject they are rule 7 helpers on the participle under rule 86, a participle being a token that carries subordination; are realizes the copular lexeme itself and takes the head under rule 9. The expressed subject ta ploia is already spent on the ships, so the supplied they belongs here under rule 76's availability test rather than being added.
Expressed conjunction to and, coordinating the two concessive participial clauses.
Agentive preposition to by under rule 36; the noun it governs has no determiner, so nothing else competes.
Anarthrous noun to winds; variant SBLGNT.JAS.3.4.v003 is underdetermined and the projection's base reading is compatible, so no textual decision is made here under rule 12.
Attributive adjective to rough, split from its noun under rule 26.
Passive participle expanded into a finite clause; the auxiliary are is its helper under rule 9 and the head is the lexical driven under rule 17.

Main verb with its auxiliary *are* and the phrasal particle *about*, which is part of `μετάγω`'s own English gloss rather than a preposition governing anything, so rule 36 does not move it. The supplied correlative *yet* answers the supplied *though* of s006 and is taken as a rule 7 helper on the clause it introduces, standing inside the main clause it marks. Rules 88 and 82 do not reach this and are not cited for it: rule 88 is scoped in terms to a participle converted into a COORDINATE FINITE clause, and this is a subordinate concessive with a matrix verb, while rule 82's corpus units all have a Greek token in each clause answering to the correlative, which `μετάγεται` does not. The competing reading gives *yet* to `ὄντα` as the discontinuous second half of *though … yet*, on rule 27's ground that a helper stays with what licenses it and that the corpus spells one token's correlative as a discontinuous English pair; JHN.7.19 marks such a *yet* `added`, though a `καί` stood there. This chapter's `yet` is the corpus's only one on a plain finite indicative, so no precedent settles it and rule 16 records the alternative here.
Second agentive/instrumental hypo to by under rule 36.

Superlative adjective rendered very small, headed on small under rule 17, very spelling only the elative degree; the supplied determiner goes to the noun under rule 58, both Greek words being anarthrous.
Noun takes the discontinuous supplied determiner a … rudder under rules 15 and 58.
Relative adverb to whither.
Article to the under rule 19. Variant SBLGNT.JAS.3.4.v004 is underdetermined with the base among the compatible readings, so rule 12 leaves it as projected.
Noun stands alone beside its own article.

Substantival article whose participle the ASV renders by the agent noun steersman rather than by a relative clause, so no pronoun or relativizer is written for it; the article keeps the English determiner with the case preposition riding along under rule 21, headed on the under rule 17's on the clause. Rules 32 and 90 do not reach this: they give the article a pronoun or a single relativizer, and the ASV supplies neither here, leaving the ordinary determiner reading. Rule 22's whole-phrase reading is likewise out, since the participle's own English word carries the nominal.
Participle of euthynō rendered by the agent noun steersman, which is the whole of its English realization.
Finite verb to willeth.

review_notes: Reviewed and left unchanged: all 21 source ids and all 31 target ids are partitioned exactly once, every unit is aligned with nonempty arrays, and every head is a member of its own array (rules 1 and 3).

Three notes were expanded to record reasoning the accepted version left implicit — the s006 supplied subject under rule 76, the s012 particle about under rule 36, and the s019 exclusion of rules 32, 90 and 22 — but no unit's membership, status or head was changed.

s019 is the unit most worth a second reader's attention. tou euthynontos is a substantival article before a participle, which normally splits under rule 32 with the article taking a pronoun; here the ASV nominalizes the participle into the agent noun steersman and writes no pronoun and no relativizer, so rule 90's one-word case does not arise either and the article is left with the plain determiner plus its case preposition under rules 21 and 17. The alternative of leaving the article unrepresented and giving of the steersman whole to the participle is refused because a determiner the article can anchor is written.

Two genuine judgment calls stay recorded in their units under rule 16: the head of telikauta (great over so) and the placement of the correlative yet (on the main verb metagetai rather than on the participle onta that carries the supplied though). Rule 99's what manner of precedent is the strongest pull toward a head on so, and was considered and set aside because great is a gloss of the lexeme's magnitude sense rather than a supplied generic completion.

Neither variant unit is marked FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE, and both are underdetermined with the projected base among the compatible readings, so rules 12 and 97 leave the projection untouched and nothing here is added on textual grounds.
